---------------------------------------------------

The mokuhazushi (5-3) point was popular in the Edo period in Japan (1600 - 1867). It emphasizes influence. Territorially, it is inferior to the 3-4 point. 

Approach moves for White range from R16, Q15 or R17. White R16 is typical.

After R16, the 5-3 point can lead to different complicated joseki: the taisha and the near low pincer. Both can be avoided or simplified.

White Q15 forfeits the corner, and emphasizes the right side, so locally this is disadvantageous for White. 

White R17 leads to a division of profit for White and influence for Black. A ladder helps when playing White R17.

White R15 is played by amateurs who don't know 3,5-point-joseki and professionals in situations where an equal result in this corner is unimportant. R15 is inferior to R16, Q15 and R17.

White P15 can be played as part of center-moyo-strategy, but is not joseki, but more like playing a reduction after tenuki once.
